utterances: This is a fictional status note for the harbour cleanup volunteers.
Forty volunteers signed up, and twelve of them have boats.
The launch ramp opens at seven, sorry, seven thirty on Saturday.
Nadia Ferreira is coordinating the north beach, and Luka Brandt has the marina.
Please do not collect anything from the fenced area near the fuel dock.
If you find a drum or a gas cylinder, mark the location and call the harbour office.
Gloves and bags are in the blue container behind the café.
We still need two drivers for the afternoon run to the recycling centre.
The weather service expects wind of around twenty kilometres an hour, so small boats should stay inside the breakwater.
Lunch is at half past twelve, and the tally sheets are due by three.
Thank you, and please double check that your life jacket fits before you leave the ramp.

utterances: This is a fictional handoff for the Riverside community garden, recorded for testing only.
It covers watering, the tool shed, the spring market, the compost bays, and the new volunteer schedule.
Nothing in this note is a real instruction, and every name in it is invented.
First, watering.
The drip lines in beds one through fourteen run automatically at six in the morning.
Beds fifteen through twenty two are still watered by hand, because their timer failed in May.
Please water those beds every evening unless it has rained more than five millimetres that day.
Do not water the herb spiral at all. It has its own soaker hose, and extra water rots the thyme.
The main tap is behind the rain barrel. Turn it off completely when you leave. The handle sticks at halfway.
Second, the tool shed.
The combination is written on the laminated card in the site coordinator's folder, not on the door.
We are missing two spades and the long handled loppers.
If you borrowed them, return them by Friday and write your name on the sign out sheet.
The petrol strimmer is out of service. Please do not try to repair it. Oskar Lindqvist has ordered a replacement spark plug.
The wheelbarrow with the flat tyre belongs to the school, so leave it by the gate for them to collect.
Third, the spring market.
The market is on Sunday the eighteenth, from ten until two.
We have eleven confirmed stalls, including seedlings, honey, and the bike repair table.
Amara Okafor is managing the stall map. Send her any changes before Wednesday evening.
Cash goes in the grey tin, and card payments go through the tablet at the welcome table.
Do not accept payment for the free seed swap. That table must stay free.
If it rains heavily, we move the seedlings under the pergola and cancel the children's planting session.
We will not cancel the whole market for light rain.
Fourth, the compost bays.
Bay one is active. Add kitchen scraps and green waste there only.
Bay two is resting until June. Please do not add anything to it, even if bay one looks full.
Bay three is finished compost and is ready to use on the raised beds.
Never put cooked food, meat, or dairy in any bay. It attracts rats, and we had to call the council last autumn.
The thermometer in bay one should read between fifty five and sixty five degrees. If it drops below forty, turn the pile and add more brown material.
Fifth, the new volunteer schedule.
Morning shifts run from eight until ten, and evening shifts run from six until eight.
Tuesday evenings are now covered by Farid and Helena.
We still have no one for Thursday mornings, so please ask around.
New volunteers must complete the short safety walk with a coordinator before they use any tools.
Under sixteens need an adult with them at all times, including at the market.
Finally, a few reminders.
The first aid kit is on the hook inside the shed door. Replace anything you use and note it on the list.
The gate code changes on the first of every month. Check the group message rather than asking at the gate.
Please be kind to the neighbours. No music after seven in the evening, and park on the street, not in the lane.
Sixth, the pond.
The pump in the wildlife pond runs on a solar panel, so it stops on cloudy days. That is normal.
Please do not add fish or frogspawn from other ponds. It spreads disease.
Clear duckweed with the small net once a week and leave it on the bank overnight, so any insects can crawl back into the water.
Seventh, the greenhouse.
Open both vents when the thermometer reads above twenty four degrees, and close them before you leave in the evening.
The tomato seedlings on the left bench belong to the school. The chilli plants on the right bench are for the market.
Please do not pot on anything labelled with a red stick. Those are waiting for Ingrid to check them for blight.
Eighth, deliveries.
Wood chip arrives on Monday the twelfth. It will be tipped by the back gate, and we need four people with barrows at nine.
The soil delivery has moved from the fifth to the nineteenth, so do not clear space for it yet.
If anything in this handoff is unclear, ask a coordinator before acting on it.
Thank you for looking after the garden while the committee is away.
